modules.title: Computer Fundamentals & Digital Operations
modules.summary: Hardware architecture, OS file trees, document engineering, digital hygiene, and safe handling of 22-digit cryptographic keys.

lessons.title: Hardware, Operating Systems & File Architecture
lessons.content:
Every digital workspace relies on the coordination between physical hardware (CPU, RAM, NVMe/SSD storage, and peripherals such as printers and scanners) and the Operating System (Windows, Linux, macOS).

Key Operational Rules:
1. Directory Hierarchy: Keep project folders lowercase without spaces (e.g., kuts_global_academy) so they deploy cleanly across Windows workstations, Linux servers, and IPFS UnixFS trees.
2. Open Document Standards: Prefer plain Markdown (.md), UTF-8 JSON (.json), and archival PDF/A for long-term readability independent of proprietary software versions.
3. Local Backup Discipline: Maintain at least two physical copies of critical project directories before pinning them to decentralized networks.

lessons.title: Digital Hygiene & 22-Digit Cryptographic Key Safety
lessons.content:
In passwordless cryptographic systems like KUTS Category 04 (Neural), your 22-digit Base-100 serial key is your identity.

Security Best Practices:
- Never share your Category 04 access key in public chat groups or unencrypted screenshots.
- Store keys inside an encrypted password manager or an offline hardware backup.
- Verify domain URLs (e.g., pinaleaf.com or verified DNSLink gateways) before entering cryptographic payloads.

options: To ensure cross-platform compatibility across Linux servers and case-sensitive IPFS gateways

modules.title: IT, Networking & Decentralized IPFS Web
modules.summary: IPv4/IPv6 addressing, DNS, REST APIs, Git workflows, and pinning/retrieving immutable CIDs on IPFS.

lessons.title: Location Addressing (HTTP) vs. Content Addressing (IPFS)
lessons.content:
Traditional websites use HTTP URLs (Location Addressing): your browser asks a specific server at an IP address for a file. If that server goes offline or alters the file silently, the link breaks or misleads.

IPFS (InterPlanetary File System) uses Content Addressing:
- Every file or directory is hashed cryptographically into a Content Identifier (CID, e.g., bafybeig...).
- If even a single comma inside a lesson changes, the CID changes completely.
- Any node pinning that CID can serve the verified content to learners anywhere in the world.

lessons.title: Packaging & Pinning Static Bundles with DNSLink
lessons.content:
To deploy a database-free application on IPFS:
1. Use relative paths (./index.html, ./data/catalog.json) so the bundle works under any gateway path.
2. Package the directory into a Content Addressable Archive (CAR) or run 'ipfs add -r kuts_global_academy'.
3. Point a _dnslink TXT DNS record on your domain to /ipfs/<ROOT_CID> so users visit a memorable domain while receiving cryptographically verified IPFS blocks.

quiz.q: What happens to an IPFS Content Identifier (CID) if a single character inside the file is modified?
options: The CID stays the same but increments a version number
A completely new cryptographic CID is generated
IPFS automatically deletes the old file

quiz.q: Which DNS mechanism maps a human-readable domain name to an immutable IPFS CID?

modules.title: Data Science & Temporal Ledger Analytics
modules.summary: Structured schemas (JSON, CSV, Parquet), Python scripting, Julian Day Number (JDN) conversion, and Base-100 payload verification.

lessons.title: Structured Data & Floating-Point Precision Rules
lessons.content:
Clean data pipelines depend on strict schemas (JSON, CSV, Parquet) and exact numeric types.

Under KUTS Revision 8 Section 3.2a:
- Calendar instants are converted to Julian Day Numbers (JDN) on the proleptic Gregorian calendar (1 BCE = astronomical year 0).
- Sub-second precision must be carried at full IEEE-754 double precision (at least 15 significant digits) before dividing by Session-Epoch (334.00 ns) and rounding to the nearest integer.

lessons.title: Base-100 Positional Decomposition
lessons.content:
Once the integer Session-Epoch tick count N is calculated, it is decomposed into 11 two-digit Base-100 fields (00 to 99), yielding 22 decimal digits.

This structure provides 100^11 = 10^22 distinct temporal positions, spanning approximately 105.8 million years from Reference Origin T0 while preserving fixed-width lexicographical sorting.

modules.title: Artificial Intelligence & Applied GenAI
modules.summary: Machine learning fundamentals, LLM tokenization, prompt engineering, Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG), and RVE compute token metering.

lessons.title: LLM Tokenization & Resource-Verification Metering
lessons.content:
Large Language Models (LLMs) process text in sub-word chunks called tokens rather than whole words. Both input prompt tokens and generated output tokens consume real electrical energy and GPU compute.

In the KUTS Kine Valuation Equation (Section 2.6):
- Baseline Identity: 1 Kine (K) = 10 kWh of industrial energy + 0.1M (100,000) AI compute tokens (with w1 = 0.5, w2 = 0.5, w3 = 0).
- Token metering must be captured from verifiable serving infrastructure logs rather than self-reported estimates.

lessons.title: Grounding AI with Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG)
lessons.content: To prevent hallucinations in enterprise and scientific workflows, RAG retrieves verified source passages (such as pinned IPFS specifications) and injects them into the model's context window before generating an answer.

quiz.q: Under the KUTS baseline valuation identity (w1=0.5, w2=0.5), what resources equal 1 Kine (K)?
options: 10 kWh of energy + 0.1M (100,000) AI compute tokens
100 kWh of energy + 10M AI compute tokens

quiz.q: What is the primary purpose of Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG)?
options: To ground AI responses in verified reference documents and reduce hallucinations
To compress video files for IPFS
To replace HTML with binary machine code

modules.title: Future Technologies & Cyber-Physical Systems
modules.summary: Autonomous tool-calling AI agents, edge IoT telemetry, post-quantum cryptography, and multi-scalar chronometry.

lessons.title: Cyber-Physical Anchor Nodes & Light-Distance Scaling
lessons.content:
Cyber-physical systems bridge physical hardware sensors with deterministic digital ledgers. In KUTS, time (Tn) and light-distance (Dn = Tn × c) are locked together across 64 decimal orders.

At Order 38 (Session-Epoch, 334.00 ns), light travels approximately 100.1 meters. Distributed anchor nodes measure propagation delay relative to Master Origin Node THRINC000 to maintain synchronization within one Session-Epoch tick.

lessons.title: Autonomous Agents & Human-in-the-Loop Governance
lessons.content: Next-generation AI systems combine reasoning models with deterministic software tools (calculators, ledger verifiers, IPFS pinners) bounded by strict conformance checks and human oversight.

quiz.q: Approximately how far does light travel during one KUTS Session-Epoch (Order 38 = 334.00 ns)?
What is the maximum synchronization error bound allowed between two connected KUTS nodes for uniqueness purposes?
options: Less than one Session-Epoch tick (334.00 ns)

modules.title: KUTS Rev 8 Engineering & GRL Operations
modules.summary: 16 Functional Categories, GW150914 worked verification, atomic sub-tick allocation, and Least Action Governance.

lessons.title: Composite Identifier Grammar & GW150914 Verification
lessons.content:
Every KUTS Revision 8 Composite Identifier follows the strict grammar:
[2-Digit Category]:[11 Base-100 Fields]-[Anchor Node ID].[2-Digit Sub-Tick]

Verified Scientific Benchmark (GW150914 — 14 Sept 2015, 09:50:45.39 UTC):
- Elapsed time from T0 = 379,147,341,045.39 seconds
- Session-Epoch ticks N = 1,135,171,679,776,616,766
- Composite Identifier: 03:00.01.13.51.71.67.97.76.61.67.66-THR.01

lessons.title: Atomic Sub-Tick Allocation & Least Action Governance
lessons.content:
1. Sub-Tick Uniqueness (§4.3): Each node allocates slots 00–99 atomically within a single 334.00 ns tick (~2.99 × 10^8 events/sec/node). Overflow queues to the next tick or escalates to Order 32 Register-Epoch (0.334 ps).
2. Historical Immutability (§5.3): Committed identifiers are never deleted or silently edited; corrections emit a new Category 11 reclassification record.
3. Least Action Governance (§2.5 & §6.5): Category 12 Kine settlements automatically allocate 1.5% to Protocol Fiscal Sweep (PFS) and 1.5% to Regenerative Stewardship Pool (RSP), crediting 97% net to the recipient.
